# 2 Baruch Chapter 25 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 25 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 25:1 — "kept / preserved"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "you-also will-be-kept" | Literal Syriac: "be kept/guarded" |
| LOGOS | "you also will be preserved" | Formal English for divine protection |
| PNEUMA | "you too will be kept safe" | Expanded for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "preserved." Conveys the sense of divine protective keeping more fully than bare "kept."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 25:2 — "dread and confusion / terror and confusion / terror and chaos"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "dread-and-confusion" | Hyphenated compound following Syriac noun pair |
| LOGOS | "terror and confusion" | Standard formal English pair |
| PNEUMA | "terror and chaos" | More vivid modern pair |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "terror and confusion." "Confusion" is more precise — the Syriac term suggests disorder/confusion rather than abstract chaos.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Lexical precision.

---

## 25:3 — "say in their thoughts / say in their hearts / cry out in their hearts"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "say in-their-thoughts" | Syriac uses a thought/mind term, not heart |
| LOGOS | "say in their thoughts" | Preserves the distinction |
| PNEUMA | "cry out in their hearts" | Shifts to heart and adds vocal intensity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "say in their hearts." The Syriac term can refer to inner deliberation; "hearts" is a standard Semitic idiom for the seat of thought. PNEUMA's "cry out" overstates.

**Status:** Resolved as LOGOS with minor adjustment. "Hearts" preferred over "thoughts" for Semitic idiom.

---
